lessons.title: Predict before you listen
lessons.summary: Use the reading time to predict the type of answer for every gap and underline the key words.

lessons.title: Follow the signposts
lessons.summary: Recognise the phrases speakers use in Parts 2 and 4 to show that a new point, and the next answer, is coming.

lessons.title: Don’t fall for distractors
lessons.summary: Spot corrections, rejected options and changed plans, and wait for the final answer before you write.

lessons.title: Hear the paraphrase
lessons.summary: Match the words in the question to the different words speakers use, especially in multiple choice and matching.

lessons.title: Spelling, numbers and dates
lessons.summary: Write spelled names, phone numbers, dates, prices and postcodes exactly, and avoid the classic teens-and-tens mistakes.

lessons.title: Keep to the word limit
lessons.summary: Learn exactly what counts as a word and a number, so that a right answer is never marked wrong for being too long.

lessons.title: Part 4: lecture note completion
lessons.summary: Follow the headings, predict each gap and keep up with a ten-question lecture with no break in the middle.

lessons.title: Skimming and scanning
lessons.summary: Read for the big picture in two minutes, then find exact details without reading every word.

lessons.title: Spotting paraphrase
lessons.summary: The answer rarely uses the question’s words: learn the six ways the test rewrites an idea.

lessons.title: Tracking reference words
lessons.summary: Follow this, which, such, it, the former and the latter back to what they mean, so ideas connect across sentences.

lessons.title: True, False or Not Given
lessons.summary: A 3-step decision tree that separates FALSE from NOT GIVEN, plus the qualifier traps that cost Band 7 candidates marks.

lessons.title: Yes, No or Not Given
lessons.summary: Judge statements against the writer’s opinions, not the facts, by learning to spot the language of views and claims.

lessons.title: Matching headings
lessons.summary: Find each paragraph’s controlling idea first, then eliminate headings that only match a detail or borrow its words.

lessons.title: Matching information: which paragraph contains…?
lessons.summary: Scan for the type of information — a reason, an example, a comparison — not the topic, and expect the answers in any order.

lessons.title: Matching features: people, dates and places
lessons.summary: Find every mention of each name first, note what each person says, then match the paraphrased statements.

lessons.title: Matching sentence endings
lessons.summary: The completed sentence must be grammatical and say what the passage says — eliminate endings that are true but do not complete that beginning.

lessons.title: Multiple choice: predict, match, eliminate
lessons.summary: Answer the question before you read the options, then prove every wrong option wrong: too broad, too narrow, reversed or mentioned but not the answer.

lessons.title: Sentence, summary, note, table and flow-chart completion
lessons.summary: Predict the word class, obey the word limit, copy the spelling exactly and check the grammar of the finished sentence.

lessons.title: Diagram labelling and short-answer questions
lessons.summary: Follow the description in the text step by step to label a diagram, and let the wh- word tell you what kind of short answer to write.

lessons.title: Timing the Reading test
lessons.summary: A 17 / 20 / 23-minute plan for the three sections, the 2-minute rule, and the order to tackle question types.

lessons.title: Extending your answers
lessons.summary: Turn one-line replies into developed answers with Answer → Reason → Example → Contrast, and judge the right length for Part 1 and Part 3.

lessons.title: Natural discourse markers
lessons.summary: Use the small spoken phrases that make you sound fluent and connected — and stop overusing the written linkers that make you sound like an essay.

lessons.title: Pauses, thinking time and missing words
lessons.summary: Make your pauses sound like thinking about ideas rather than searching for words, buy time naturally, and talk your way round a word you do not know.

lessons.title: Mixing tenses for grammatical range
lessons.summary: Use past simple for stories, present perfect for experience, used to and would for past habits, and conditionals for hypotheticals — accurately and naturally.

lessons.title: Part 2: planning and telling a story
lessons.summary: Use the one-minute preparation for keywords, not sentences, and shape your two-minute talk like a story so it sounds natural rather than memorised.

lessons.title: Clarity over accent
lessons.summary: What the Pronunciation criterion really rewards, and the four habits that make you easy to understand: word stress, sentence stress, chunking and clear endings.

lessons.title: The overview paragraph comes first
lessons.summary: Write a clear, number-free overview of the two main features straight after your introduction: the single biggest step from Band 7 to Band 8 in Task 1.

lessons.title: Trends and comparisons in line and bar charts
lessons.summary: Group the data, describe change with precise trend language and compare categories, without a single opinion or reason.

lessons.title: Proportions, tables and mixed charts
lessons.summary: Turn percentages into natural proportion language, pick the right figures from a busy table and link two charts in one report.

lessons.title: Maps and processes
lessons.summary: Describe where things are and how they changed with location language and the passive, and walk through a process stage by stage with clear sequencing.

lessons.title: Getting the tone of a letter right
lessons.summary: Choose formal, semi-formal or informal from the reader, then match the opening, closing, phrasing and structure to that choice.

lessons.title: Phrases for six types of letter
lessons.summary: Ready-to-adapt language for complaints, requests, apologies, invitations, thanks and explanations, at formal, semi-formal and informal levels.

lessons.title: The five Task 2 essay types
lessons.summary: Recognise each essay type from its wording, count the parts of the question, and use a paragraph plan that answers every part.

lessons.title: The Band 8 essay method
lessons.summary: A ten-step method for Task 2: analyse, plan, take a clear position, develop one idea per paragraph in depth, and proofread against a checklist.

lessons.title: Building a body paragraph with PEEL
lessons.summary: Point, Explain, Example, Link: develop one idea fully, and watch a Band 6 paragraph become a Band 8 one.

lessons.title: Cohesion without mechanical linkers
lessons.summary: Hold your writing together with reference words, substitution, topic sentences and contrast structures instead of a linking word at the start of every sentence.
